text:
maria: quick heads-up — got an OSS alert (oss-alerts) for a transitive CVE in tls-util pulled in by our KMS client used in Private deployments. need a one-page handoff checklist for oncall so they can mitigate fast. tagging +eng-sre +eng-platform. :wave:

alex: saw it. initial creds: CVE-2026-xxxx, affects tls-util < 2.1.3, severity looks High by NVD. question: is this library only used by the private KMS client or elsewhere?

maria: primarily bundled into the kms-client binary we ship to private customers; also in a small internal helper used by eng-platform for key rotation tooling. not in hosted runtime.

jamie: platform note — we own the packaging/upgrade pipeline for kms-client. security should own triage severity & customer comms. propose quick ownership map: platform = patch/build/rollout, eng-sre = infra canary & deploy, sec = triage + comms + mitigations. can we codify that into a tiny handoff checklist?

sarah: oncall perspective: need steps we can follow in 15-30m without deep context. suggested minimal mitigation flow below. i tested the rotate-keys flow in staging yesterday so it's doable.

maria: ok here's a first-draft checklist — please edit inline. i put it as plain text so people can paste into incidents:

```
Handoff checklist: transitive CVE affecting KMS client
1) Triage
  - Confirm CVE identifier & affected versions (NVD, OSS advisory).
  - Confirm which deployed binaries include the vulnerable package (kms-client, rotate-tool).
  - Classify attacker surface (does exploit require network access? local?).
2) Impact & scope
  - Query inventory: run `./scripts/find-binaries --package tls-util --version <range>`
  - Map to customers with private deployments (use `infra-catalog` tag kms-client:v*).
3) Short-term mitigations (oncall actionable)
  - If exploit requires direct access to customer network, notify customers immediately.
  - Rotate KMS keys for affected customers (eng-sre can run rotation if delegated).
  - Apply RBAC restriction: temporarily revoke nonessential service principal scopes for kms-client.
  - Enable audit logging at DEBUG for KMS proxy to capture suspicious access (retain logs to secure bucket).
4) Patch & rollout
  - Platform: bump dependency -> build -> smoke tests -> publish kms-client vX.Y.Z.
  - Eng-sre: canary rollout to 1-2 private clusters, monitor latency/error; escalate rollback criteria.
5) Post-incident
  - Security: prepare comms, CVE summary, mitigation steps for customers.
  - Add regression tests (dependency fuzz + integration) to prevent re-introduction.
6) Ownership & escalation
  - Security lead on call = point for severity decisions and comms.
  - If customer impact > 5% or data-exfil possibility -> page oncall lead + infra director (P0).
```

alex: looks solid. couple of additions: include an explicit step to capture and snapshot current KMS policies (so rotate can be reversed if needed) and a quick gh command to create a dependency PR template. e.g. `gh pr create --title "deps: bump tls-util to 2.1.3" --body "CVE-2026-xxxx"`.

jamie: agreed. i'll own the PR/CI side. i'll also add a short smoke-test checklist to the rollout doc. linking internal doc once updated: https://redwood.internal/docs/security/kms-cve-handoff (WIP).

sarah: oncall action items assigned: create ticket SEC-4521, set priority P1, tag eng-platform, eng-sre. i've added the temporary RBAC restrict step to the ticket.

sec-bot: created issue SEC-4521. assignee: jamie. priority: P1. labels: cve, kms, oncall-action.

maria: perfect — i'll fold this into the triage playbook under "transitive dep -> kms client" and pin the quick checklist to the channel. once jamie has the PR and build, can we add a note in the ticket with canary targets?

jamie: yes — will post canary targets + smoke results in SEC-4521. planning a canary at 1800 UTC, unless someone objects.

alex: no objections from eng-sre. recommend running audit-log export before canary so we have baseline.

maria: thanks all. i'll update the internal docs and post the short checklist snippet in #eng-oncall too. :thumbsup:
